question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay for config, tool, and system defaults, or keep immutable baselines in conformance-only Policy and Nix-managed config surfaces?
rationale: The request changes security enforcement, config precedence, runtime write failures, status/doctor reporting, and upgrade expectations, while current main only provides adjacent conformance checks plus Nix-managed config immutability.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

options.title: Keep conformance-only surfaces
options.body: Document Policy, policy compare, attestations, and Nix-managed config as the supported operator baseline story while runtime config remains mutable outside Nix mode.

options.title: Defer for hook design
options.body: Leave the issue open until related policy-hook proposals settle whether enforcement belongs in plugin hooks or core config/write paths.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the issue and authored the prior exact implementation candidate, making them the clearest owner for the security-boundary choice.
